text:
alex: Heads-up — hit a routing quirk in prod around model alias + compatibility headers. Tenant sent X-Model-Alias: gptx-8q and X-Compat: strict and gateway routed to gptx-9 (newer) which fails on kv-cache shape.
min: hmm. can you paste the raw headers and rule that matched?
alex: sure — request looked like:
```
POST /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood.ai
X-Tenant-ID: tenant-42
X-Model-Alias: gptx-8q
X-Compat: strict
```
Routing rule for the route is: `match: path:/v1/generate, header:X-Model-Alias` then resolve alias -> alias points to [gptx-9, gptx-8q-q] ordered by default.
taylor: why would alias resolution prefer gptx-9 if tenant asked for gptx-8q explicitly? sounds like alias semantics are wrong.
sara: maybe the header is treated as an alias token and we still do alias canonicalization which can reorder? we intended tenant header to either be a direct model id or an alias lookup, but not both.
alex: exactly — for this tenant gptx-8q is both an alias and a concrete variant in the alias set. gateway did alias lookup and returned the highest-priority variant (gptx-9) ignoring X-Compat.
min: two problems: alias->variant ordering should respect compatibility constraints, and header precedence rules need clarity. Proposal: add an explicit header namespace — X-Model-Id (exact) vs X-Model-Alias (alias lookup). if we get X-Model-Id we skip alias resolution.
taylor: agreed on separate header names. but we also need rule-level compatibility enforcement: routing rule should be able to declare `compatibility: require-strict` so resolution filters variants that don't match compat metadata.
sara: we already have compat metadata on model entries (quantization, kv-shapes, runtime tag). routing resolver currently uses a heuristic scoring function that doesn't consider `require` flags. change sounds reasonable.
min: UX note — console currently exposes an "alias edit" and a "route pin" control. Users confuse pin vs alias. If we add X-Model-Id vs Alias, we should also update rollouts UI: pin-to-id should set a route-level override that forbids alias-fallbacks.
taylor: telemetry ask — add a metric for "alias-resolution-path" (direct-id | alias->variant | compatibility-fallback) so we can see how often strict compat prevents a chosen variant. also log tenant header precedence decisions.
alex: +1. I hit this because fallback to newer model caused a regression. We should also have a soft-fail mode: if compatibility mismatch detected, try pinned quantized variant; if nothing matches, return 409 with helpful message rather than silently pick a risky variant.
sara: agree on erroring when `compatibility=require` and no variant matches. For `compatibility: prefer` we can fallback and emit an alert.
min: implementation plan: (1) add header name disambiguation (X-Model-Id vs X-Model-Alias) in gateway parser, (2) update alias resolver to accept a compat filter param, (3) route DSL: add `compatibility: [require|prefer|ignore]`, (4) console: expose pin-to-id UX and tooltip + telemetry toggle.
taylor: can we keep backwards compat for tenants currently setting X-Model-Alias? maybe treat previous header as alias by default, but new header is explicit id. document the change in changelog and set a grace period.
min: yep — default behavior preserved for 30 days; new behavior opt-in via header. We'll add a knob in console to opt-in per-route.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: alias-resolver-v2 -> canary on prod cluster cluster-a at 2026-03-22T03:00Z.
alex: thanks. small follow-ups: add e2e test that sends X-Compat: strict + alias that contains both quantized and float variants, assert resolver picks only compat-safe variants or returns 409.
sara: i'll own the console copy/tooltip. taylor, can you add the telemetry counter to the routing trace?
taylor: on it — will add `alias_resolution.reason` tag and counter `routing.alias_resolution_total{reason=...}`
min: ok let's slot this into next sprint. assign PRs after design doc. :thumbsup:
